title: pvTableToStructuredGrid
body:
## pvTableToStructuredGrid

Turns a table into a curvilinear structured grid: X, Y and Z columns give the point coordinates, row order is point order with i varying fastest, then j, then k, and the other columns become point arrays. WholeExtent gives the grid's index ranges, and the table must have exactly (imax-imin+1)(jmax-jmin+1)(kmax-kmin+1) rows. Use it for gridded data exported row by row, e.g. a CSV of a structured solver block; use pvTableToPoints for scattered points.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- With the ParaView default WholeExtent [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] only a one-row table fits; always set the extent to match the table.
- Rows must be ordered i fastest; a table sorted differently gives a scrambled grid.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `TableToStructuredGrid`. Identity: `filters/TableToStructuredGrid`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input. Accepted data: tables (rows and columns) (vtkTable). The input needs at least one row (table) array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkTable"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WholeExtent` | Index ranges of the structured grid as [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax] (inclusive point indices). The number of points, (imax-imin+1)(jmax-jmin+1)(kmax-kmin+1), must equal the number of table rows, or ParaView reports an error and produces nothing. For a 2-D grid keep one range collapsed, e.g. kmin = kmax = 0. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `XColumn` | This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the X coordinate in the generated polydata dataset. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `YColumn` | This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the Y coordinate in the generated polydata dataset. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `ZColumn` | This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the Z coordinate in the generated polydata dataset. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
